lanes.lane: Fine-line tattoo artist websites + quiet-luxury / editorial-minimal aesthetics + Pinterest fine-line branding references
techniques: editorial serif/sans pairing
single-accent color restraint
generous whitespace rhythm
unified neutral photo treatment
calm lowercase microcopy

libraries: GSAP 3 + ScrollTrigger (CDN, no build) - scroll-reveal, pinned sections, headline reveals
Lenis (CDN) - inertial smooth-scroll that pairs with ScrollTrigger for the buttery 'đỉnh liền mạch' feel

findings.name: Atelier Eva (Brooklyn fine-line / micro-realism studio)
findings.what: Leading fine-line + micro-realism studio site. Note: the LIVE site is now pure black-and-white sans-serif (Neue Haas Grotesk), centered text-first hero, generous whitespace, gallery via Instagram-grid embeds, booking via a Typeform 'Create Your Tattoo' CTA repeated in nav + hero + artist cards. Its widely-cited 'serif + beige, gallery-like' phase still circulates in design roundups (fontsinuse documents the custom Florentine-based logotype) and is the more useful reference for Pully.
findings.takeaway: Two lessons: (1) the calmest version wins - one repeated booking CTA, huge whitespace, zero decoration; (2) the earlier serif+warm-neutral identity is closer to Pully's brief than the current cold mono version, so Pully can occupy the 'warm editorial gallery' space Atelier Eva vacated.
findings.apply: Keep Pully's Cormorant + ivory warmth (it is the differentiator). Repeat ONE booking CTA consistently (nav 'Book', hero 'Book an appointment', and a closing band) using identical wording. Treat the artist bio page like a gallery wall: portrait + name in Cormorant + tiny tracked specialties line, lots of air. Avoid live Instagram embeds - they break the unified photo treatment; host curated images instead.

findings.name: Dr. Woo (single-needle fine-line pioneer)
findings.what: The reference fine-line artist; built reputation almost entirely on a consistent, restrained image feed - intricate single-needle work shot on neutral skin against quiet backgrounds, minimal captions.
findings.takeaway: For fine-line, the WORK photographed consistently is the entire brand. A coherent, neutral, watermark-light image set out-performs any UI flourish. Captions are short and quiet.
findings.apply: Define a strict image spec for Pully's gallery feed (see photo-treatment finding) and apply it to all 3D modes so every piece in the floating cloud / curved-wall / tunnel reads as one body of work. Keep lightbox captions to 1 short line in tracked sans (motif + placement), nothing salesy.

findings.name: Photographing fine-line work for a unified portfolio (Cocreate / Lume Cube guides)
findings.what: Practical specs from tattoo-photography guides: soft diffused light at 45deg to avoid glare, neutral matte background (matte black / neutral grey / raw studio wall), 4000-5000K neutral white, keep the setup consistent across shots, avoid over-saturation and skin-smoothing.
findings.takeaway: Consistency of background, light temperature and crop is what makes a portfolio look 'editorial' rather than 'a phone gallery'. The image set, not the website chrome, carries the quiet-luxury feel.
findings.apply: Standardise every gallery image: same warm-neutral / charcoal backdrop, soft 45deg light, ~4500K, tight consistent crop, no heavy filters. In code, give all gallery textures a uniform subtle treatment (slight desaturation + faint film grain via a CSS/WebGL overlay) so even mixed-source photos cohere. Add a small, low-opacity 'pully.ink' watermark in one fixed corner only.

findings.name: Awwwards editorial-layout & minimal collections (Cormorant + asymmetric grids)
findings.what: Award-winning editorial portfolios pair a stunning serif (Cormorant specifically called out) with a simple sans, hold an 'incredibly light interface through negative space and asymmetrical grids', and use large headlines with rhythmic spacing that guide the eye.
findings.takeaway: Award-quality minimal = expressive serif + huge negative space + deliberate asymmetry + scroll rhythm, NOT more effects. 'Quietly confident' beats busy.
findings.apply: Break the current centered symmetry in About/Signatures: set the section title off to one column, captions small and tracked in the other; use unequal column widths. Add Lenis + GSAP ScrollTrigger so headlines reveal line-by-line (SplitType) and sections fade/translate in on scroll - this delivers the 'đỉnh liền mạch' buttery feel without a bundler.

findings.name: Lass Tattoo (Webflow, 'tranquil not edgy' minimal)
findings.what: Cited as a model of what clean minimal design does for a solo fine-line artist - tranquil rather than edgy, restrained palette, clear portfolio organization.
findings.takeaway: A solo fine-line artist reads as premium by being calm and well-organised, not dark/grungy. Clear named categories beat one big undifferentiated grid.
findings.apply: Pully already has the right category language (Botanical / Lettering / Animals / Symbols / Keepsakes). Let those filter the gallery (tap a Signature -> gallery shows that motif). Keep tone tranquil: avoid heavy shadows, neon, or aggressive motion.

findings.name: Hanoi fine-line scene + Vietnamese type support (Silver Ant, OCD Ink, Vietcetera)
findings.what: Hanoi's fine-line peers (Silver Ant ~32K IG, OCD Ink, H2M, LaThanh) lead with minimalist/ornamental work and an Instagram-first presence; most have functional-but-generic sites.
findings.takeaway: The local competitive bar is low on web craft - a genuinely editorial, buttery site is a real differentiator for Pully in Hà Nội. Vietnamese diacritics must render perfectly everywhere.
findings.apply: Lean into the gap: ship the polished motion + unified gallery the locals lack. Confirm Be Vietnam Pro covers all diacritics for body/labels, and verify Cormorant Garamond renders Vietnamese display text (ữ, ọ, ấ, etc.) - if any glyphs fall back, restrict Cormorant to Latin/brand words and set Vietnamese display in a diacritic-safe serif. Keep place name 'Hà Nội' and address fully accented.

findings.name: Premium tattoo booking-as-request pattern (Venue.ink / Tattoo Studio Pro)
findings.what: Premium studios use a custom request form (placement, size, reference upload, a few words on the idea), artist approves/declines before confirming, and a deposit filters non-serious enquiries - framed as a seamless step, not friction.
findings.takeaway: For a curated artist, booking should feel like applying to be tattooed, not buying a ticket. The 'request -> artist confirms' framing reinforces exclusivity and is the honest model for one solo artist.
findings.apply: Reframe Pully's form copy from 'Book an appointment' to a quiet 'Request a session' / 'Tell me about your piece'. Fields: name, contact (IG/Zalo), motif/category, placement, approx size, a few words, optional reference upload, preferred month. End with 'I review every request personally and reply within a few days.' Show the deposit as a calm one-liner, not a paywall. Calendar shows month availability as a soft signal (open/limited), confirmation still goes through Pully.

findings.name: Single-red-accent strategy for fine-line branding (Pinterest 'Red Fine Line Tattoo' + 2026 soft-accent trend)
findings.what: Pinterest fine-line boards show the on-trend move: predominantly black/grey linework with a single soft red/coral accent (a red star, one red bloom). 2026 reporting frames this as 'soft color accents replacing fully saturated work, keeping the minimalist aesthetic intact'.
findings.takeaway: The single-red accent is literally Pully's tattoo style mirrored in the UI - the brand and the artwork share one rule: one restrained red against quiet black/ivory. That coherence is the whole identity.
findings.apply: Codify a strict red budget in CSS: red appears ONLY on (1) the active/hover state of the single primary CTA, (2) one italic Cormorant accent word per section max, (3) the calendar 'open' dot / availability tick, (4) a 1px link underline on hover. Everything else stays ivory/charcoal. Use #C8362A as-is; reserve #E0594B only for hover lift. The restraint makes each red moment feel intentional, exactly like one red bloom in a black-line bouquet.

Verdict up front: skip the React/Tailwind component MCPs for THIS site (they need a bundler), but the magic MCP's logo_search is still usable, and there is a strong stack of true drop-in CDN libraries + CC0/MIT assets that fit the fine-line "quiet luxury" brief perfectly.

findings.name: 21st.dev (component marketplace)
findings.what: Community marketplace of polished UI 'blocks' (heroes, galleries, CTAs, marketing sections) and components.
findings.takeaway: Beautiful, but every component is React + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + Radix — it assumes a JSX/Tailwind build. It is NOT drop-in for a vanilla HTML/CSS/JS site.
findings.apply: NEEDS A BUILD STEP. Do not wire it into Pully directly. Use it for visual inspiration only — browse hero/gallery/booking-form layouts, then hand-port the look in plain HTML/CSS. Porting a single component's CSS by hand is realistic; adopting the library is not without migrating to Vite/Next.

findings.name: magic MCP — 21st_magic_component_builder / _inspiration
findings.what: 21st.dev's MCP server: natural-language -> generated React/TS + Tailwind + shadcn component, plus an inspiration browser. Freemium (~5 free gen/mo, $20/mo).
findings.takeaway: Output is React/Tailwind code, same build-step problem as the marketplace. The _inspiration tool returns JSON/snippets you can read for ideas without committing code.
findings.apply: NEEDS A BUILD STEP for its main output. For Pully, use 21st_magic_component_inspiration as a research/mood tool only; don't paste its JSX into the static site.

findings.name: magic MCP — logo_search
findings.what: Same magic MCP, but this tool returns brand logos/icons and CAN output raw SVG (not just JSX/TSX).
findings.takeaway: This is the one part of the magic MCP that IS no-build-friendly because SVG pastes straight into HTML.
findings.apply: DROP-IN VIA SVG. Use logo_search(format:'SVG') to grab the Instagram / TikTok / Facebook icons for Pully's contact + booking footer as clean inline SVG you can recolor to charcoal #141009 or the red accent #C8362A.

findings.name: GSAP 3.13 + ScrollTrigger
findings.what: Industry-standard animation + scroll-trigger toolkit. Since Webflow's acquisition, GSAP and ALL plugins (ScrollTrigger, SplitText, etc.) are 100% free for commercial use as of v3.13 (April 2025).
findings.takeaway: Framework-agnostic, loads via a plain <script> tag, no build needed. The single biggest upgrade lever for 'award-quality' on a static site. (Only restriction: can't use it to build a Webflow competitor — irrelevant here.)
findings.apply: DROP-IN VIA CDN. Add <script src='https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.13.0/dist/gsap.min.js'></script> + the ScrollTrigger build, then gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger). Drive Pully's section scroll-reveals, hero text stagger, parallax on About imagery, and pinned transitions between the 3 gallery modes. Use SplitText (now free) for line-by-line Cormorant headline reveals.

findings.name: Lenis smooth-scroll
findings.what: Tiny, modern smooth-scroll that keeps native DOM scroll (good for accessibility/INP) instead of hijacking it.
findings.takeaway: This is what makes a site feel 'liền mạch'/buttery. Loads via CDN in one line and syncs cleanly with GSAP ScrollTrigger.
findings.apply: DROP-IN VIA CDN (unpkg.com/lenis). Init Lenis, then bridge it: lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update); gsap.ticker.add(t=>lenis.raf(t*1000)); gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0). Gives Pully the cinematic, weighted scroll a premium portfolio needs. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by skipping init.

findings.name: OGL (lightweight WebGL)
findings.what: Minimal WebGL library by Nathan Gordon, much smaller than Three.js, ships as an ES module.
findings.takeaway: If the 3D gallery is the only heavy WebGL need, OGL can power image-hover distortion shaders far more cheaply than another Three.js scene. Honestly: Pully already loads Three.js via importmap, so for the gallery itself stick with Three; reach for OGL only for lightweight standalone shader hovers if you want to avoid a second Three scene.
findings.apply: DROP-IN VIA CDN (importmap entry to cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/ogl). Use for a subtle liquid/displacement distortion on lightbox thumbnails so fine-line tattoo images 'ripple' on hover — restrained, matching quiet-luxury.

findings.name: Motion (motion.dev)
findings.what: Animation library built on native browser APIs (WAAPI); ~1/7th GSAP's size, can run off the main thread, usable in vanilla JS via CDN ESM.
findings.takeaway: A lighter alternative for simple enter/hover animations. GSAP is still the better pick for Pully's complex timelines/ScrollTrigger; mention as the lean option if bundle weight ever becomes a concern.
findings.apply: DROP-IN VIA CDN (ESM import). Optional. Could handle small UI micro-animations (button press, calendar day hover) while GSAP owns the cinematic scroll work. Don't load both unless justified.

findings.name: Codrops demos (ImageTrail, ImageReveal, RepetitionHover, custom cursor)
findings.what: Tympanus/Codrops publishes the actual source for high-end effects: ImageTrailEffects, ImageRevealHover, RapidImageHoverMenu, RepetitionHoverEffect, AnimatedCustomCursor — mostly vanilla JS.
findings.takeaway: These are exactly the editorial/fashion micro-interactions Pully wants, and the downloadable demo CODE is MIT-licensed (free for commercial use, full modification). Caveat: design freebies/images bundled in demos may NOT be resold/redistributed — swap in Pully's own tattoo photos.
findings.apply: DROP-IN (copy vanilla JS/CSS, swap assets). Use ImageReveal/RepetitionHover on the Signatures + nav links; AnimatedCustomCursor for an SVG fine-line cursor (a thin ring that morphs/grows over gallery items, tinted #C8362A); ImageTrail optionally on the hero. Pull source from each repo's GitHub.

findings.name: Hover.css
findings.what: 100+ CSS-only hover effects (2D transitions, underline sweeps, glow, border) prefixed hvr-. MIT for personal/open-source use.
findings.takeaway: Zero-JS, single CSS file from CDN — the safest possible drop-in for button/link polish. Note licensing nuance: MIT covers personal/OSS; Ian Lunn sells a separate commercial license, so for a paid client deliverable confirm the license (for a personal birthday gift the MIT path is fine).
findings.apply: DROP-IN VIA CDN (cdnjs hover.css/2.3.1). Apply restrained underline-sweep (hvr-underline-from-center) to nav + booking CTA in the red accent. Use sparingly — pick 1-2 effects so it stays 'quiet luxury', not flashy.

findings.name: Cormorant Garamond + Be Vietnam Pro (Google Fonts, Vietnamese subset)
findings.what: Pully's chosen pair. Confirmed: both expose a 'vietnamese' subset on Google Fonts; Be Vietnam Pro was purpose-built with refined Vietnamese diacritics, and Cormorant includes Vietnamese Unicode ranges.
findings.takeaway: The current type choice is correct and free. The key is loading the vietnamese subset so Hà Nội diacritics render perfectly.
findings.apply: DROP-IN VIA CDN. In the Google Fonts <link>, ensure the vietnamese subset is included and add &display=swap. Use Be Vietnam Pro for all Vietnamese body/UI copy (booking form, calendar) and Cormorant for English/Latin display headings.

findings.name: Viaoda Libre (Google Fonts)
findings.what: Free display serif by a Vietnamese designer, inspired by Vietnamese cultural symbolism/script; works for titles and small text.
findings.takeaway: A meaningful, on-brand optional accent face that ties the 'editorial' look to PULLY's Vietnamese identity — a thoughtful birthday-gift detail.
findings.apply: DROP-IN VIA CDN (optional). Consider for one signature moment — e.g. the artist's name 'PULLY' or a single section title — to add Vietnamese character without disrupting the Cormorant/Be Vietnam Pro system. Use once, not everywhere.

findings.name: feTurbulence SVG grain / noise overlay
findings.what: Native SVG filter (feTurbulence + feColorMatrix) that generates resolution-independent film-grain/paper noise with no image asset.
findings.takeaway: The cleanest way to add the warm-ivory 'paper' tactility and a subtle grain that reads as premium print — inline, tiny, free, no HTTP request.
findings.apply: DROP-IN (inline SVG + CSS). Add a fixed full-viewport overlay div with the feTurbulence filter at very low opacity (~3-6%), mix-blend-mode multiply over the #F7F3EC ivory, so the whole site feels like fine art paper. Generate/tune with frontend-hero.com/css-noise-generator or uwarp.design/nnnoise.

findings.name: Noise/grain generators (nnnoise, Frontend Hero, Ultimate Design Tools)
findings.what: Free online tools that output copy-paste SVG/CSS noise with adjustable grain size, color, and opacity.
findings.takeaway: Lets you dial the exact subtle grain for Pully rather than hand-writing feTurbulence params.
findings.apply: DROP-IN (generated CSS/SVG). Tune a single grain value, then paste once. Also see freecodecamp.org/news/grainy-css-backgrounds-using-svg-filters for the technique writeup.

findings.name: FreeSVG.org / SVG Silh / Rawpixel (CC0 fine-line + botanical motifs)
findings.what: Public-domain/CC0 vector sources: FreeSVG.org and SVG Silh release under CC0 (copy/modify/commercial OK); Rawpixel has CC0 public-domain botanical/floral line art and vintage illustration.
findings.takeaway: Truly free decorative fine-line/botanical SVG motifs for section dividers, corner ornaments, and the booking card — CC0 means no attribution and commercial-safe. (Avoid Etsy/Vecteezy 'free' items that carry per-license restrictions.)
findings.apply: DROP-IN (inline SVG, recolor to currentColor). Use a delicate single-line botanical sprig as a section divider and a thin ornamental flourish under the 'PULLY' wordmark; recolor strokes to charcoal with one accent stroke in #C8362A. Inline them so you can animate stroke-dashoffset draw-on with GSAP.

lanes.lane: Open-source GitHub repos & code techniques for Three.js / WebGL image galleries and smooth scroll — usable from CDN without a bundler, tailored to PULLY's static Three.js (importmap, jsdelivr) build.
libraries: Lenis (smooth scroll) — CDN: https://unpkg.com/lenis@1.3.23/dist/lenis.min.js + https://unpkg.com/lenis@1.3.23/dist/lenis.css — MIT, ~4KB gz, NO bundler needed
GSAP + ScrollTrigger — CDN: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3/dist/gsap.min.js + https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3/dist/ScrollTrigger.min.js — standard 'no charge' license, NO bundler needed
OGL (minimal WebGL lib, ESM) — CDN: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/ogl@1.0.11/+esm (use via importmap like the existing three entry) — license: Unlicense (public domain), NO bundler needed
Three.js 0.161.0 — already in the project via importmap (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.161.0/build/three.module.js) — MIT
curtains.js (HTML DOM -> WebGL textured planes) — CDN available on jsdelivr/unpkg (npm 'curtainsjs') — MIT, NO bundler needed (alternative to writing raw Three.js plane sync)
techniques: Velocity-driven vertex bend: read smoothed scroll velocity into a uniform, offset plane vertices in Z with a sine curve across screen-space UVs (the signature 'curved film' look)
Circular/cylinder layout via JS: position.y = cos((x/widthTotal)*PI)*R - R so planes arc; wrap 'extra' offset by total width for infinite loop
lerp smoothing of target scroll -> current scroll for buttery motion even without Lenis (used by Codrops galleries)

Lenis + GSAP single-RAF sync: lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update); gsap.ticker.add(t => lenis.raf(t*1000)); gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0) — one loop drives smooth scroll, ScrollTrigger, and the WebGL render
data-lenis-prevent attribute on the booking-form / lightbox / scrollable modal so smooth-scroll hijacking doesn't break inner scroll
Mood/atmosphere background: per-image color palette interpolated by scroll depth + film grain in a fullscreen shader (ties to PULLY's ivory/charcoal/red accent)
GSAP ScrollTrigger pin + scrub + snap for a horizontal pinned gallery section
Hover chromatic aberration / directional 'magnetic push' distortion computed in fragment shader by pixel distance to mouse

findings.name: darkroomengineering/lenis (formerly studio-freight/lenis)
findings.what: The de-facto smooth-scroll library used on most award-winning sites. ~4KB gz, MIT, zero deps. Wraps native scroll so position:sticky, anchor links and a11y keep working.
findings.takeaway: This is the single highest-impact 'seamless/buttery' upgrade and it is a pure drop-in CDN script — no build step. It exposes scroll velocity, which is exactly the signal the WebGL gallery wants.
findings.apply: Add the CDN <script>/<link> to index.html. Init new Lenis(), then sync GSAP: lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update); gsap.ticker.add(t=>lenis.raf(t*1000)); gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0). Feed lenis velocity into the gallery's existing 3D modes as a uniform for subtle drift/bend. Put data-lenis-prevent on the booking form and the lightbox so inner scroll still works.

findings.name: Codrops — Infinite Circular Gallery (OGL + GLSL) + repo lhbizarro/infinite-circular-webgl-gallery
findings.what: Canonical tutorial + MIT repo for a curved/cylinder infinite gallery driven by drag + wheel. Planes arc via position.y = cos((x/widthTotal)*PI)*R - R; a uSpeed uniform warps vertices on fast scroll.
findings.takeaway: This is the reference implementation for the 'curved-wall orbit' mode you already have. The math (arc positioning + infinite wrap by total width + velocity warp) is directly portable to Three.js, and it shows how to make scroll feel physical.
findings.apply: Port the arc-position + infinite-wrap logic into the existing curved-wall mode in gallery.js. Add a uSpeed uniform fed by Lenis velocity to bend planes during fast scroll, then settle. Tune R and segment count so it reads as a delicate cylinder, not a carnival ring — fits the 'quiet luxury' brand. (Repo uses webpack but the technique is bundler-agnostic; reimplement against the project's existing three import.)

findings.name: bizarro — infinite-webl-gallery (linear) + infinite-circular-webgl-gallery
findings.what: Two MIT reference repos (OGL + GLSL) for infinite auto-scrolling galleries — one flat/linear, one circular. Includes the lerp-smoothed target-scroll pattern and velocity-to-distortion uniforms.
findings.takeaway: Best minimal, readable source for the core 'infinite loop + smooth + distort' loop without framework noise. The linear one is a clean basis for a 'depth tunnel'/strip mode.
findings.apply: Lift the scroll-lerp loop (target vs current, multiply delta into a uSpeed uniform) into the project's render loop so even the floating-cloud and tunnel modes inherit weighty, smoothed motion. Keep distortion amplitude low for fine-line elegance.

findings.name: Codrops — Scroll-Reactive 3D Depth Gallery + repo houmahani/codrops-depth-gallery
findings.what: Feb/Mar 2026 Three.js tutorial: smoothed scroll velocity drives parallax, scroll-drift, a 'breath' tilt/scale, plus mood-based background that interpolates each image's 3-color palette as you move through depth, with film grain.
findings.takeaway: Most current, on-trend reference and it maps perfectly onto your existing depth-tunnel mode. The palette-interpolation background is a premium touch that can be themed to ivory/charcoal with the single red accent.
findings.apply: Adopt the velocity->parallax/drift/breath layering for the depth-tunnel mode. Replace its rainbow palettes with PULLY's: background blobs in warm ivory #F7F3EC over charcoal #141009, with the #C8362A accent bleeding in only on fast scroll (brightness/accent lift). Add a faint film-grain shader pass for editorial texture. (Uses Vite; technique is portable — reimplement in the static build.)

findings.name: Manishbhai9350/Curvy-Project-Showcase
findings.what: Three.js portfolio where scroll velocity bends 3D project cards (sine-based Z bend across screen-space UVs) plus a post-process fragment 'magnetic push' toward the mouse and procedural edge noise. Demo: https://curvy-project-showcase.onrender.com/
findings.takeaway: Great visual target for a click-to-expand portfolio card that bends as it grows — could elevate your lightbox/expand interaction beyond a flat modal.
findings.apply: Use its expand-while-bending idea for the lightbox: when a gallery image is selected, animate it into a slightly curved plane (GSAP-tweened bend uniform) rather than a hard cut. Pairs with the mouse-push distortion for a tactile feel. Note: repo requires Vite, so treat as a technique reference, not a copy-paste — reimplement the shader against three.

findings.name: martinlaxenaire/curtainsjs
findings.what: MIT vanilla WebGL lib that turns existing DOM elements into shader-animated WebGL planes that stay synced to the DOM on scroll/resize. Supports post-processing, FBOs, hover/scroll distortion (e.g. chromatic aberration).
findings.takeaway: An alternative architecture: keep real, accessible, SEO-friendly tags in the DOM and add WebGL distortion on top — lower risk than fully custom geometry, and it handles scroll-sync jank for you. CDN-ready, no bundler.
findings.apply: If a fully custom Three.js gallery feels heavy to maintain, use curtains.js for the gallery grid: real images for accessibility/fallback, with a subtle hover chromatic-aberration + scroll-velocity ripple shader in brand greys. Good progressive-enhancement fallback path if WebGL is unsupported.

findings.name: OGL (oframe/ogl)
findings.what: Minimal ES-module WebGL library (Unlicense / public domain), Three-like API but tiny. Loadable from CDN as ESM (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/ogl@1.0.11/+esm). It's the library behind the Codrops circular/linear gallery tutorials.
findings.takeaway: If gallery weight/perf matters, OGL is far lighter than Three.js for a dedicated gallery scene and the best-documented gallery tutorials are written for it — but mixing two WebGL libs adds bytes.
findings.apply: Optional: add an 'ogl' importmap entry next to the existing 'three' entry to run the Codrops circular-gallery code closer to verbatim. Otherwise prefer porting the techniques into the existing Three.js scene to avoid shipping two WebGL libraries. License (Unlicense) means zero attribution constraints.

findings.name: GSAP ScrollTrigger — horizontal pin gallery patterns
findings.what: Reference CodePens (incl. official GreenSock collection https://codepen.io/collection/DkvGzg) for pin + scrub + snap horizontal galleries: pin a section and translate a track by its scrollWidth as the user scrolls vertically.
findings.takeaway: A non-WebGL, low-risk way to add a cinematic 'editorial' moment (e.g. a horizontal 'Signatures' strip) that feels premium and pairs naturally with Lenis.
findings.apply: Wrap the Signatures or a curated 'best work' row in a ScrollTrigger pin+scrub track for a horizontal scroll beat between the 3D gallery and booking. Add snap to land cleanly on each image; keep easing slow for the quiet-luxury tone.

lanes.lane: Award-winning immersive / seamless Three.js & WebGL portfolio and gallery websites
libraries: Lenis (smooth scroll) — CDN: https://unpkg.com/lenis@1.3.23/dist/lenis.min.js + lenis.css; UMD global `Lenis`, no bundler
GSAP 3 + ScrollTrigger — CDN: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3/dist/gsap.min.js and .../ScrollTrigger.min.js; UMD globals, no bundler
Three.js (already in build via importmap) — also exposes addons: three/addons/postprocessing/{EffectComposer,RenderPass,BokehPass,UnrealBloomPass}.js via the same importmap, no bundler
OGL — lighter WebGL alt for the infinite circular gallery (CDN ESM available); only if you want a dedicated curved-gallery mode, otherwise stay on Three.js
curtains.js — vanilla WebGL DOM-plane library for image-to-3D + page-transition curtain reveals (CDN, no bundler) — optional
techniques: Lenis smooth-scroll as the single master loop, driving page scroll + a `uScrollVelocity` uniform + GSAP ScrollTrigger off one RAF tick (gsap.ticker.add → lenis.raf; gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0))

Scroll-velocity-driven vertex bend: position.y -= sin(uv.x*PI) * clamp(uScrollVelocity) * sign(uScrollVelocity) * k — the planes 'bow' as you fly through the tunnel/float, the single biggest 'seamless' upgrade

Curved/cylinder layout via trig: map x-position to rotationY (Math.PI..-Math.PI) and cos((x/total)*PI) Y-arc — upgrade the existing 'wall' mode into a true infinite circular gallery with drag inertia + snap-to-center
RGB-channel-split displacement on hover: offset red/blue UVs by mouse velocity * strength, merge with original — restrained chromatic shimmer on the focused tattoo plane
Scroll-velocity → camera scrub with GSAP ScrollTrigger scrub timeline: tie travel (0..1) to actual page scroll instead of wheel deltas, so the 3D camera and the page move as one continuous surface
In-WebGL fade reveal: full-screen black quad whose opacity is a uniform tweened by GSAP on THREE.LoadingManager onLoad — premium intro loader with no DOM flash
Depth-of-field via BokehPass in EffectComposer (addons over importmap) — focus the centered/hovered plane, blur the rest; the defining 'expensive' look for fine-line work
Inertia/lerp everywhere: scroll.current lerps toward scroll.target at ease 0.05–0.1; drag adds velocity, decays *0.94 — already partially in Pully's wall mode, extend to all input
Film grain in the fragment shader gated by interaction (uMouseEnter + uScrollVelocity) — subtle, restraint-based, matches 'quiet luxury'
Mood/palette-driven background that blends between planes by camera depth — let each tattoo's dominant tone subtly tint the charcoal void, with the single red accent as the only saturated color

findings.name: Codrops — Infinite Circular Gallery (OGL + GLSL)
findings.what: Draggable + scrollable infinite cylinder of image planes. Curvature is pure trig: map(plane.x, -total, total, PI, -PI) drives rotationY; cos((x/total)*PI)*75-75 gives the vertical arc. Inertia via lerp(scroll.current, scroll.target, 0.05); debounced onCheck() snaps the nearest item to center; an `extra` offset wraps items for true infinity. A `uSpeed` uniform feeds velocity-based bend.
findings.takeaway: This is the canonical recipe for the curved/cylinder gallery feel — the curvature and the snap-to-center are what make it read as 'premium' rather than a flat carousel.
findings.apply: Upgrade Pully's existing 'wall' mode (currently a static cylinder you orbit) into this: keep the cylinder math but add (1) lerp-based scroll target so drag has real inertia, (2) debounced snap so a tattoo always settles dead-center, (3) the cos() vertical arc so edge pieces gently dip — turning 'wall' into a signature browsable shelf of fine-line work.

findings.name: Codrops — Scroll-Reactive 3D Gallery with Velocity + Mood Backgrounds (Three.js)
findings.what: Depth-stacked planes at z = -index*gap; camera flies through Z on scroll, smoothed by lerp. A reusable scroll-velocity signal (frame delta, damped, clamped, threshold-zeroed) drives: brightness lift on fast scroll, a 'breath' tilt/pulse, and mouse parallax. Each image supplies palette colors that blend between planes by camera depth, rendered as soft smoothstep blobs + film grain. Notably uses NO Lenis/GSAP — vanilla Three.js math.
findings.takeaway: Treats scrolling as 'time passing,' not navigation — velocity becomes the central expressive signal feeding many small effects at once. That layering of micro-responses is exactly what 'đỉnh liền mạch / buttery' means.
findings.apply: Pully's 'tunnel' mode already stacks planes down -Z — add a damped velocity signal and feed it into a subtle brightness lift + a gentle plane tilt while traveling. Use each tattoo's dominant tone as a faint depth-blended tint on the charcoal background, reserving #C8362A as the only place real saturation appears (e.g. accent pieces glow faintly red as they pass focus).

findings.name: Codrops — Distortion & Grain on Scroll with Shaders (Three.js + Lenis)
findings.what: Vertex shader bows planes by scroll velocity: position.y -= sin(uv.x*PI) * min(abs(uScrollVelocity),5.0) * sign(uScrollVelocity) * -0.01 (a 'perfect bow', direction-preserving, capped). uScrollVelocity comes straight from Lenis. Fragment shader adds 2D-noise grain constrained to a cursor-following circle, blended in via mix() gated by uMouseEnter + uScrollVelocity*0.1.
findings.takeaway: The premium feel is intentional restraint: effects only fire during interaction, the displacement factor is tiny (0.01), grain is localized. Micro-distortion that enhances rather than overwhelms.
findings.apply: This is the highest-leverage change for Pully. Pipe Lenis velocity into a uScrollVelocity uniform on every gallery plane and apply the sin(uv.x*PI) bow — the float/tunnel modes will visibly 'flex' as you move, the core seamless upgrade. Add the cursor-circle grain only on the hovered plane so fine-line ink gets a tactile paper-grain shimmer without muddying the linework.

findings.name: Codrops — Motion Hover Effects with Image Distortions + RGB Shift (Three.js)
findings.what: Computes a plane's velocity (position - previousPosition) and uses it as a distortion offset (×strength). The RGB-shift variant displaces the red and blue channels by separate UV offsets driven by mouse position/velocity, then merges with the original texture. Curved distortion via sin() with UVs ×PI.
findings.takeaway: Velocity-as-offset is a tiny, reusable primitive that produces a responsive, alive surface; channel-split RGB shift adds a restrained 'chromatic' luxury accent on hover.
findings.apply: On hover over a tattoo plane (Pully already raycasts on pointer), apply a slight RGB-split keyed to pointer velocity — the focused piece gets a delicate shimmer that resolves to crisp when still. Keep strength very low so black/grey linework stays legible; this reads as fashion-editorial polish, not glitch.

findings.name: Lenis (darkroom.engineering) — smooth scroll, CDN/no-bundler
findings.what: Buttery smooth-scroll via UMD CDN (unpkg lenis.min.js + lenis.css). Init `new Lenis()`, drive with rAF or, better, sync to GSAP: lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update); gsap.ticker.add(t => lenis.raf(t*1000)); gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0). Recommended buttery settings: lerp ~0.1 (lower = smoother), duration ~1.2, wheelMultiplier 1, custom easing.
findings.takeaway: Lenis is the spine of nearly every Awwwards 'seamless' site — it unifies page scroll, WebGL scroll, ScrollTrigger and parallax into ONE loop, killing the disjointed feel of separate scroll handlers. Works fully without a build step.
findings.apply: Add Lenis as the master loop. Replace Pully's raw `wheel`-delta travel logic with Lenis scroll → a normalized 0..1 that scrubs the tunnel/float camera; expose Lenis velocity as the uScrollVelocity uniform feeding the bow/grain shaders. This single change makes the whole site (hero, gallery, about, booking) feel like one continuous, weighted surface.

findings.name: GSAP ScrollTrigger — scroll-driven camera scrub (CDN)
findings.what: ScrollTrigger links a timeline directly to the scrollbar with `scrub`, so camera position/rotation animate in lockstep with scroll progress (see GreenSock's official Three.js camera CodePen: codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/MWBvQRW). Loadable purely via CDN (gsap.min.js + ScrollTrigger.min.js), pin sections, scrub timelines, snap to labels.
findings.takeaway: scrub + pin is how award sites choreograph a 3D camera move to feel like a film that you scrub frame-by-frame — deterministic, reversible, perfectly synced to the page.
findings.apply: Pin the gallery section and drive Pully's camera travel (and the float→wall→tunnel transitions) with a scrubbed ScrollTrigger timeline instead of auto-drift + wheel. Scrolling the page then becomes a cinematic dolly through the tattoo space; mode switches can be timeline labels with snap, so each mode 'locks in' cleanly.

findings.name: Three.js official — Depth-of-Field / BokehPass via importmap addons
findings.what: EffectComposer + RenderPass + BokehPass imported from 'three/addons/postprocessing/...' using the exact importmap pattern Pully already uses (no bundler). BokehPass mimics camera focus, blurring objects off the focal plane; focus/aperture/maxblur are tweakable uniforms.
findings.takeaway: Cinematic depth-of-field is the cheapest way to make a WebGL scene look 'expensive' and photographed rather than rendered — and it needs zero new tooling on top of Pully's importmap.
findings.apply: Wrap Pully's render() in an EffectComposer and add a BokehPass focused on the centered/hovered tattoo, softly blurring the float-cloud depth and tunnel distance. Keep aperture subtle (quiet luxury). Lerp the focus distance toward the active plane so attention always falls on one piece — perfect for showcasing individual fine-line designs.

findings.name: Lusion — WebGL Scroll-Sync demo (benchmark)
findings.what: A reference-grade example of perfectly synchronized scroll + WebGL: DOM and 3D move as one, with inertia, momentum and depth that never desync. Studio-quality 'seamless' bar to aim at.
findings.takeaway: The defining quality of top WebGL portfolios isn't more effects — it's that scroll, camera, and content share one inertial system so nothing ever feels bolted on.
findings.apply: Use as the north-star feel check for Pully: after wiring Lenis + ScrollTrigger scrub + velocity uniforms, the test is whether hero → gallery → about scrolls as one continuous weighted surface. If any section's motion feels independent, route it through the same Lenis loop.

findings.name: THREE.LoadingManager — premium in-WebGL intro loader/reveal
findings.what: LoadingManager exposes onStart/onProgress/onLoad/onError to track every texture. Best-practice reveal: keep the scene black, draw a full-screen black quad over the render, and on onLoad tween its opacity uniform to 0 with GSAP — the fade happens inside WebGL so there's no DOM flash or pop.
findings.takeaway: A controlled, fade-from-black reveal tied to real asset progress is the signature 'considered' first impression of award sites; doing it in-shader avoids the cheap-feeling DOM overlay flicker.
findings.apply: Pully loads tattoo textures with TextureLoader (currently fire-and-forget). Route them through a LoadingManager, show a minimal centered progress mark (Cormorant numerals on ivory), and on completion GSAP-fade an in-WebGL black quad to unveil the gallery — replacing the current galleryLoading DOM toggle with a seamless premium intro.
